Understanding the Need

Dr. Benson Kiarie, PhDLead Facilitator | CEO, Vantage Africa

Why resource mobilisation capacity matters

Good programmes depend on sustained funding. Donor budgets are tightening, competition for every grant is rising, and funders now expect clear results logic, credible budgets, evidence of impact and locally led delivery. Organisations that cannot meet these expectations lose funding to those that can, however strong their work on the ground.

Many teams have the programme knowledge but not the proposal skills: they struggle to map the right donors, structure a concept note, articulate a Theory of Change, build a logframe or justify a budget. The result is rushed, generic applications and low success rates.

Our promise

Participants do not just listen. They draft, review and refine real outputs, and leave with a concept note, a donor map, a Theory of Change, a logframe and a resource mobilisation action plan for their own organisation.

Strong fundraising capacity changes more than income

It enables multi-year, flexible funding instead of short project cycles; helps local partners build their own donor relationships rather than depending on sub-grants; improves programme design itself, because Theory of Change and logframe thinking make interventions more coherent and measurable; and builds institutional resilience through a diversified donor base that can absorb funding shocks.

What Organisations Need from this Programme

1

Donor intelligence

Knowing who funds what, and how to reach them

2

Strong proposals

Concept notes and proposals that score well against donor criteria

3

Results logic

A credible Theory of Change and logframe behind every request

4

Credible budgets

Budgets and narratives that match the activities and results

5

Diversified funding

A resource mobilisation plan that reduces dependence on one donor

Who We Are and Why We Are Best Placed

Vantage Africa School of Leadership is a pan-African leadership, strategy and M&E capacity-building institution based in Nairobi. We work with NGOs, INGOs, faith-based organisations, government institutions and the private sector to strengthen the systems and skills that win and sustain funding: strategy, results frameworks, proposal writing and resource mobilisation.

Programme Design

The three-day Resource Mobilisation and Proposal Development Programme takes participants through the full proposal cycle, from finding the right donor to submitting a well-reviewed application. It is sequenced from understanding to application: participants first build clarity on the funding landscape and results logic, then move into hands-on drafting, budgeting, peer review and action planning.

By the End of the Programme, Participants Will Be Able To

1

Mapthe donor landscape and identify funding opportunities that match their mission

2

Developa resource mobilisation strategy that diversifies funding sources

3

Structureconcept notes and full proposals around what donors assess

4

Builda Theory of Change and a logical framework with SMART indicators

5

Preparecredible budgets and budget narratives linked to activities and results

6

Reviewproposals against donor criteria and plan their next 90 days of fundraising

Our Methodology

Our methodology is a chain of learning: read the concept, see a real example, draft your own version, get peer feedback, revise, and connect it to a live funding opportunity. Participants leave with usable drafts and tools, not notes alone. The approach below is indicative and is confirmed with each client at the discovery meeting.

1

Context review

Before the programme

  • Discovery meeting with the client
  • Review of strategy, past proposals and funding mix
  • Pre-test of every participant
Needs assessment and baseline
2

Concept input

Days 1–3

  • Short 20–30 minute inputs
  • Real donor calls and winning proposals
  • Examples from the client's sector
Clear concepts
3

Live drafting

Days 1–3

  • Small groups of 4–6
  • Structured templates
  • Facilitators coach every group
Drafts on real opportunities
4

Peer review

Day 3

  • Donor-style scoring rubric
  • Critique, refine and strengthen
  • Plenary on common mistakes
Revised, stronger drafts
5

Action planning

Day 3

  • 90-day resource mobilisation plan
  • One live opportunity per team
  • Post-test and evaluation
Action plans and report
6

Follow-up

Optional, up to 90 days

  • Review of real proposals
  • Coaching on live applications
  • Progress check on plans
Proposals submitted

1

2

Pre- and post-test, and scoring of drafts against donor criteria

3

4
Results

Proposals submitted and funding secured after the programme

Three-Day Programme Agenda

Each day ends with a concrete output that feeds into the next. Day 1 finds the right donors, Day 2 designs the results logic and turns it into a concept note, and Day 3 costs it, reviews it against donor criteria and commits to a 90-day plan. The programme can be delivered in person or virtually; the virtual version uses breakout rooms, live drafting on shared screens and low-bandwidth tools.

Day 1

Find the money

  • Opening, expectations and pre-test
  • Resource mobilisation versus fundraising
  • Funding trends and donor priorities
  • Diversifying income sources
  • Mapping and profiling donors
  • Reading a call for proposals

Donor mapping worksheet; 3–5 priority opportunities

Day 2

Design and write

  • Problem and solution trees
  • Building a Theory of Change
  • Logframes and SMART indicators
  • Concept note structure
  • Problem statement and objectives
  • Live drafting in groups

Theory of Change, logframe and draft concept note

Day 3

Cost, review and act

  • Budget structure and cost categories
  • Budget narratives and value for money
  • Peer review with a donor rubric
  • Revising the concept note
  • 90-day action plans
  • Post-test, evaluation and certificates

Revised concept note, budget and action plan

Tailored to Your Organisation

A generic fundraising course is not what organisations need. Before delivery we review each client's strategy, programmes and past proposals, and anchor every example, case study and exercise to its sector and its donors. Where possible, exercises use live or recent calls for proposals, so the drafts participants produce can be submitted.

How We Adapt the Programme by Sector

1

NGOs and INGOs

Institutional donors, consortia, sub-granting and compliance requirements.

2

Peace and humanitarian

Do No Harm, conflict sensitivity and locally led language in every proposal.

3

Faith-based organisations

Church networks, diocesan structures and faith-based funders.

4

Community organisations

Simple tools that grassroots teams can use with small grants and local donors.

5

Public institutions

Development partner funding, budget support and public–private partnerships.

6

Education and research

Research grants, scholarships and institutional partnerships.

What the Client Receives

DeliverableWhat it contains
Training agenda and session plansObjectives, activities, timings and outputs for every session
Training materials packageSlides, reading notes and worked examples from the client's sector
Participant toolkitDonor mapping tool, proposal, ToC, logframe and budget templates, review rubric
Learning evidencePre- and post-test results, output scores and attendance
Training reportLearning outcomes, output quality, gaps and recommendations
